o1.biggest_strength: It chains the emails on the real triggers: first task leads to the repeat email, and the recurring task leads to the second-device email. Fallback send days, skip rules, platform branching and a no-two-emails-a-day rule make it ready to load into the tool.
o1.biggest_mistake: Email 5 asks everyone to share a list, a habit that retains only 34% and that the tool can't trigger on or skip. It brings back a gentler team invite in the slot most worth spending on the two winning habits or on revenue.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace the share email with one that serves the two habits or a segmented Pro email. Pick one subject line per email instead of listing parenthetical test alternates.

o2.biggest_strength: Every email chases one of the two retention habits, and the team invite is dropped completely. Pro moves to day 14 and goes only to users who have hit a habit, so the series protects revenue without spending a slot on sharing.
o2.biggest_mistake: The second-device email goes on fixed day 3 instead of firing off the recurring-task trigger. That is a missed chance to sequence the two habits, and the welcome email has no mobile tailoring.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Trigger email 3 on 'recurring task created', with day 4 or 5 as the fallback, and give the welcome email a mobile line, so the series uses every trigger the tool offers.

reason: Both are calm, on-brand and built around repeats plus a second device. Output 2 is cleaner: one subject per email and a goal and measure under each. It also drops the team email entirely and keeps a well-targeted Pro ask, where Output 1 spends its last slot on sharing.
